chunks: 863 - And ʿAbdullāh ibn Faḍālah narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh and Abī Jaʿfar, peace be upon them, who said: I heard him saying:

When a boy reaches three years of age, he is told: Say, ‘There is no god but Allah,’ seven times. Then he is left until he completes three years, seven months, and twenty days, then he is told: Say, ‘Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah,’ seven times. Then he is left until he completes four years, then he is told: Say seven times, ‘May Allah bless Muḥammad and his family.’ Then he is left until he completes five years, then he is told: Which of them is your right and which of them is your left? When he knows that, his face is turned toward the qiblah and he is told: Prostrate. Then he is left until he completes seven years. When he completes seven years, he is told: Wash your face and your hands. When he has washed them, he is told: Perform salat (prayer). Then he is left until he completes nine years. When he completes them, he is taught wudu (ablution), and he is struck for it, and he is commanded to perform salat (prayer), and he is struck for it. Then when he learns wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer), Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgives him and his parents, if Allah wills.

key_terms.اسْجُدْ: prostrate; the instruction to perform sajdah
key_terms.الْغُلَامُ: the boy; the child being trained in religion
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction of prayer toward which the child is turned
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: the declaration of tawhid, affirming that there is no god but Allah
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the testimony to the Messengerhood of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.وَلِوَالِدَيْهِ: and his parents; indicating shared divine forgiveness connected to the child’s learning

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe teaching a child salat (prayer) and wudu (ablution) step by step?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines a gradual method for training a child in foundational belief, devotion, and ritual practice. It presents staged instruction in tawhid, the risalah of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, salawat, orientation to the qiblah, sajdah, wudu (ablution), and salat (prayer), showing the importance of structured religious upbringing in childhood.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.863 - Abdullah ibn Fadalah narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) and Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that He said:

"When a boy reaches the age of three, he should be instructed to say 'la illaha illa Allah (swt)' seven times.
Then he is left until he completes three years, seven months, and twenty days, at which point he is instructed to say 'Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (sw)' seven times.
He is then left until he reaches four years of age, after which he is instructed to say seven times, 'May Allah (swt) bless Muhammad and his family.'
He is then left until he turns five years old and is asked: 'Which hand is your right and which is your left?' When he recognizes this, his face is turned toward the Qiblah, and he is told to prostrate.
He is then left until he turns seven years old, at which point he is told to wash his face and hands. When he washes them, he is told to pray.
He is then left until he reaches the age of nine. At nine, he is taught the proper way of performing ablution (wudu) and is disciplined for neglecting it. He is also instructed to perform prayer and disciplined for neglecting it.
When he has learned wudu and prayer, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, forgives him and his parents, if Allah (swt) wills."
